newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Soymeal supply will rise to meet world meal demand.
newsitem.headline: Soymeal supply will rise to meet world meal demand.

text.p: The rising world demand for protein meal will have to be met by higher production of soymeal from the U.S, Brazil and Argentina, an analyst said on Monday.

Brian Rutherford, former president of the Grain and Feed Trade Association in Britain, said at a feed ingredients meeting in Singapore world meal consumption will rise to 100-105 million tonnes by 2005 from the 1992-1996 average of 84 million tonnes.
"Today's main exporters, the USA, Argentina and Brazil, will have to cover the majority of this growth," he said.
Most of the growth in consumption will come from Asia.
"It seems that having more money to spend means that it is spent on more food and especially more meat," Rutherford added.

With economic growth in Asia expanding by an average of five percent annually, this "will result in a significant increase in purchasing power and will allow many consumers to turn to better and higher valued food products," he said.
China will lead the way, with per capital meat consumption seen rising to 60 kg beyond 2000 from 40 kg at present.
